definition: A walk cycle's five main poses (Contact, Down, Pass, Up, Contact) are spaced roughly three frames apart from each other, but a sub-event nested inside that spacing - the heel snapping from a heel-first contact down to a fully flat foot - happens far faster, in about one frame, not gradually across the three.
purpose: Give the walk cycle's timing a second, faster tier most descriptions of the five-pose vocabulary leave out: the poses themselves are evenly-ish spaced, but at least one event inside that spacing is much quicker than the spacing itself.
visible_effect: The five main poses read as an even, roughly-three-frame rhythm; independently, the foot's heel-to-flat transition at each contact is a near-instant snap rather than a gradual roll across those same three frames.
psychological_or_gameplay_effect: A heel-to-flat transition spread out gradually across the full pose spacing instead of snapping quickly reads as mushy or floaty contact, even if the main poses themselves are timed correctly.
physical_interpretation: The heel-to-flat foot roll is a short mechanical event (the ankle rotating the foot flat once weight commits) riding on top of the much longer stride rhythm - two different timescales in the same cycle, not one uniform timing.
use_cases: setting initial key spacing for a new walk cycle's main poses
timing the foot-roll sub-event inside an existing walk cycle's contact pose, independent of the main pose spacing
non_use_cases: a stylised or cartoony walk that deliberately holds or drags the foot roll for comic timing rather than snapping it
a run cycle, where the overall pose spacing and the flight phase change the whole timing picture (see continuous_ground_contact_except_during_flight_phase, W03 video 26)
interactions: walk_cycle_vertical_drop_is_arrested_fall (W03, video 26) - the same five-pose vocabulary; this entry adds a timing/spacing number to poses that entry only described by shape

the foot-roll detail from W03 video 26's notes (heel peels off the ground around the ball) - this entry gives the heel-to-flat portion of that same foot roll a specific sub-frame timing the earlier video did not state
cadence_representation: Directly measurable today. ai/motion.js MEASUREMENTS.key_density already reports keys per frame from existing track key times, which is exactly what an even roughly-three-frame pose spacing would show up as; the much faster heel-to-flat sub-event would show as a locally denser key cluster inside that same series. Nothing currently distinguishes a walk cycle's main-pose spacing from a foot-roll sub-event as two different named timescales within one key_density read - that classification is not built, only the raw density measurement is.
control_surface: sample_motion / key_density already returns the raw per-frame key spacing; nothing labels a fast cluster within it as a foot-roll snap specifically.
detection_and_measurement_methods: Real: key_density (ai/motion.js MEASUREMENTS) reports keys per frame from existing track key times. Classifying which keys belong to the main-pose tier versus a faster sub-event tier (like a heel snap) is not built - it would need a declared role per key (main pose vs. sub-event) that the raw density measurement does not carry.
failure_modes: spreading the heel-to-flat transition evenly across the full pose spacing instead of snapping it quickly, which reads as mushy contact
keying the five main poses at uneven or arbitrary spacing with no consistent rhythm
roblox_considerations: None beyond the shared keyframe/track model.
examples: "when you do a walk cycle... you usually put that [pose] every three frame[s] - so we have the contact position, the down, passing position, up position, and contact again, and then you repeat" - video @ 05:15-05:27

the heel snap, contrasted with that spacing: "I want to make sure the heel is [flat] during the contact position... this part is really quick, doesn't happen in three frames, basically almost in one frame, and [the heel] snaps down" - video @ 09:12-09:34
evidence_status: video: https://youtu.be/ynXadXE9UjU @ 05:15-05:27 and @ 09:12-09:34 - stated directly by the presenter (Alessandro Camporota) while live-keying a walk cycle in 3D animation software; auto-captions are rough throughout this video (heavy accent) but these two specific numeric claims are unambiguous in context; cross-checked against this session's read of ai/motion.js MEASUREMENTS.key_density; experimental until validated
